input.command:
python3 -c "
import numpy as np

data = {
    2:  {'means': [0.5267, 0.4460, 0.5528], 'stds': [0.1905, 0.1984, 0.1402]},
    6:  {'means': [0.3899, 0.4217, 0.4092], 'stds': [0.1153, 0.1341, 0.1197]},
    12: {'means': [0.3057, 0.3568, 0.3051], 'stds': [0.1017, 0.1119, 0.1050]},
    22: {'means': [0.2684, 0.2768, 0.2577], 'stds': [0.1029, 0.0905, 0.0922]},
    44: {'means': [0.3007, 0.2724, 0.2898], 'stds': [0.1116, 0.1146, 0.1366]},
    66: {'means': [0.4071, 0.4067, 0.4067], 'stds': [0.0017, 0.0014, 0.0016]},
}

print(f'{'Count':>5} {'Batch SD':>10} {'Seed SD':>10} {'Ratio':>8}')
print('-' * 38)
ratios = []
for count, d in sorted(data.items()):
    stds = np.array(d['stds'])
    means = np.array(d['means'])
    batch_var = np.mean(stds**2)
    batch_sd = np.sqrt(batch_var)
    seed_sd = np.std(means, ddof=1)
    seed_var = seed_sd**2
    ratio = batch_var / seed_var if seed_var > 0 else float('inf')
    ratios.append(ratio)
    print(f'{count:>5} {batch_sd:>10.4f} {seed_sd:>10.4f} {ratio:>8.1f}')

print()
print(f'Mean ratio: {np.mean(ratios):.1f}')
print(f'Range: {min(ratios):.1f} -- {max(ratios):.1f}')
# Excluding count 66
ratios_no66 = ratios[:-1]
print(f'Mean ratio (excl. 66): {np.mean(ratios_no66):.1f}')
print(f'Range (excl. 66): {min(ratios_no66):.1f} -- {max(ratios_no66):.1f}')
"

\centering

\begin{tabular}{rrrr}
\toprule
\textbf{Count} & \textbf{Batch SD} & \textbf{Seed SD} & \textbf{Ratio} \\
\midrule

\bottomrule

\caption{Variance decomposition on Few-NERD (3 seeds $\times$ 25 batches per count level). Batch SD: root-mean intra-seed standard deviation averaged over seeds. Seed SD: standard deviation of per-seed means. Ratio = batch variance / seed variance. At count 66 (full schema), only one composition exists, so both components collapse to near-zero.}
\label{tab:variance_decomposition_ner}
\end{table}

Intra-batch variance dominates inter-seed variance by 5--474$\times$ on FewRel (mean 125$\times$, counts 4--64) and 10--99$\times$ on Few-NERD (mean 51$\times$, counts 2--44), confirming that random batch composition is the primary source of performance variability on both tasks, not seed-dependent randomness in model inference. The wide ratio range reflects variation in how tightly seed means cluster at each count level; even the minimum ratio (5.4$\times$ on FewRel at count 16, 10.2$\times$ on Few-NERD at count 2) indicates batch composition contributes the majority of observed variance. At count 80 (FewRel) and count 66 (Few-NERD), the full schema admits only one batch composition, collapsing batch variance by construction.
